scenes.heading: Getting paid reliably: retainers, invoicing, and late payments

sents.d: Getting paid reliably: retainers, invoicing, and late payments
A clear invoicing rhythm prevents the awkward 'did you forget to pay me' conversation.

Invoicing on a consistent schedule (e.g. the same day each month) rather than whenever you remember creates a predictable rhythm clients get used to, and makes a late payment easier to notice and follow up on quickly.

Requiring payment upfront or within a short window for new clients, before extending net-30 terms later once trust is established, protects your cash flow during the relationship's most uncertain early period.

A polite, templated follow-up message for a payment that's a few days late — sent consistently rather than only when you're frustrated enough to say something — keeps the relationship professional instead of tense.

take: Invoice consistently and follow up on late payments every time.
